_comment: Hand-labelled ground truth. `live` is the answer a careful reviewer gives with the whole corpus in front of them, and `why` is the evidence — a label without one is an opinion. Edit only with a reason recorded here.
notes: Import-less Java. Main, Service and Ledger share `package com.acme.billing`, so Main names both classes with no import at all. Service and Ledger each declare `compute`, so the name alone cannot say which one `service.compute(41)` calls: only the local's type can, and that type comes from its construction (`Service service = new Service()`). Without the Ledger decoy the corpus-unique-name fallback bound the call anyway and the fixture proved nothing. Two fences answer two questions. The dead-code verdicts on `compute` and `fee` are protected by the package-private exemption (non-private Java members are treated as exported), so they hold even without the edge. The *resolution* is fenced by W4.2: this fixture's Java rate is in `testdata/resolution_baseline.json`. Confirmed 2026-10-07 by breaking the mechanism and watching `per_language_resolution_has_not_regressed` fail with `java_same_package/java: 777 -> 555`: the construction typing has two redundant paths — the resolver binding a constructed local to its unique class, and the extractor recording a `Service{..}` initializer on the call site's local binding — and both had to be disabled before either `compute` edge was lost. `retired` is private, so it is claimable, and it is the recall label.
